I’ll eat an entire bag of chips, a family-sized pizza, or like three sleeves of cookies in one night—usually when I’m alone in my dorm. It feels like I can’t stop, even when I’m uncomfortably full. Afterward, I panic about gaining weight, so I take laxatives almost every time. I’ve been doing it for months—probably three or four times a week. It’s gotten to the point where I feel like I’m only "okay" if I’m thin. If I gain even a pound, I feel disgusting, like I’m a failure. My weight controls how I see myself, honestly. I know I’ve been sad a lot, and I don’t enjoy things like I used to, but it’s not just that. The worst part is the cycle: binge, then guilt, then laxatives, then starving myself until the next episode. It’s exhausting. I feel trapped.
D022-D013_h024.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D022-D013_h025.question: I’ve been feeling low for a few months now—just no energy, not enjoying things I used to, even spending time with my wife and watching my grandkids. I know it’s not just farming stress, though that’s hard enough—waking up before dawn, keeping up with the land. But there’s this other thing I haven’t told anyone. At least once a week, usually late at night after everyone’s asleep, I’ll go to the kitchen and eat… a lot. Like two packs of crackers, a whole loaf of bread, sometimes cold meat right from the fridge. It’s not about being hungry—it’s like something takes over. Afterward, I can’t stand how full I feel, how bloated, how *fat* I think I look, so I make myself throw it up. It’s awful, but I can’t stop. My weight’s been bouncing up and down, and I check myself in the truck’s side mirror constantly. If I gain even a little, I feel like a failure—like I’ve lost control, like I’m weak. I don’t know if it’s depression, or if this eating is making me more depressed, but the truth is, I tie my whole worth to my weight. If I’m heavier, I’m a bad man. If I’m thinner, maybe I’m okay.
D022-D013_h025.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
